```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = TRUE, message = FALSE, warning = FALSE)

# Load the dataset from your local folder
college <- read.csv("CollegeScores4yr.csv", stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
```

\vspace{2em}

## **Project Questions and Analysis**


This report analyzes institutional characteristics, costs, admissions metrics, and geographic distributions using the CollegeScores4yr dataset. Below are the ten questions analyzed using descriptive statistics and graphical methods.

\vspace{2em}




## **1. What are the central tendency and dispersion of total annual attendance cost?**

\vspace{2em}

```{r}
# Question 1: Summary statistics for annual Cost
mean_cost   <- mean(college$Cost, na.rm = TRUE)
median_cost <- median(college$Cost, na.rm = TRUE)
sd_cost     <- sd(college$Cost, na.rm = TRUE)
var_cost    <- var(college$Cost, na.rm = TRUE)
iqr_cost    <- IQR(college$Cost, na.rm = TRUE)

cat("--- Question 1: College Cost Statistics ---\n")
cat("Mean Cost:", mean_cost, "\n")
cat("Median Cost:", median_cost, "\n")
cat("Standard Deviation:", sd_cost, "\n")
cat("Variance:", var_cost, "\n")
cat("IQR:", iqr_cost, "\n\n")
```

\vspace{2em}

•	Mean Cost: $34,277.31

\vspace{1em}

•	Median Cost: $30,699

\vspace{1em}

•	Standard Deviation: $15,278.54

\vspace{1em}

•	Variance: $233,433,900

\vspace{1em}

•	IQR: $23,519.25

\vspace{3em}

## **2. What is the distributional shape and spread of admission rates?**


\vspace{2em}

```{r}
# Question 2: Admission Rate Distribution & Histogram
mean_admit   <- mean(college$AdmitRate, na.rm = TRUE)
median_admit <- median(college$AdmitRate, na.rm = TRUE)

cat("--- Question 2: Admission Rate Statistics ---\n")
cat("Mean Admit Rate:", mean_admit, "\n")
cat("Median Admit Rate:", median_admit, "\n")

# Plot a histogram for admission rates
hist(college$AdmitRate, 
     main = "Distribution of College Admission Rates", 
     xlab = "Admission Rate", 
     col = "skyblue", 
     border = "white")
```

\vspace{2em}

•	Mean Admission Rate: 67.0%

\vspace{1em}

•	Median Admission Rate: 69.5%(See histogram in generated plots showing the spread of institutional selectivity.)

\vspace{3em}



## **3. What proportions and counts of institutions fall into each control type (Public vs Private vs For-Profit)?**

\vspace{2em}

```{r}
# --- Question 3: Institutional Control Types (Categorical Analysis) ---
tbl_control  <- table(college$Control)
prop_control <- prop.table(tbl_control)

cat("--- Question 3: Institutional Control Frequencies & Proportions ---\n")
print(tbl_control)
print(prop_control)

# Plot a bar chart for Control types
barplot(tbl_control, 
        main = "Count of Institutions by Control Type", 
        col = c("steelblue", "darkorange", "gray60"),
        ylab = "Number of Colleges",
        xlab = "Control Type")
```

\vspace{2em}

•	Counts: Public (1,243), Private (599), For-Profit (170)

\vspace{2em}

•	Proportions: Public (61.78%), Private (29.77%), For-Profit (8.45%)

\vspace{3em}


## **4. How do completion rates compare across different institutional control types?**

\vspace{2em}

```{r}
# --- Question 4: Completion Rate by Institutional Control ---
mean_completion <- tapply(college$CompRate, college$Control, mean, na.rm = TRUE)

cat("\n--- Question 4: Mean Completion Rate by Control Type ---\n")
print(mean_completion)

# Plot comparative (side-by-side) boxplots
boxplot(CompRate ~ Control, data = college,
        main = "Completion Rate by Institutional Control Type",
        xlab = "Control Type", 
        ylab = "Completion Rate",
        col = c("lightblue", "orange", "lightgray"))
```

\vspace{2em}

•	Analysis using group means and comparative boxplots illustrates variations in graduation outcomes across public and private sectors.

\vspace{3em}



## **5. Is there a linear correlation between students' average SAT scores and total annual cost?**

\vspace{2em}

```{r}
# --- Question 5: Correlation between AvgSAT and Cost ---
cor_sat_cost <- cor(college$AvgSAT, college$Cost, use = "complete.obs")

cat("--- Question 5: Correlation (SAT vs Cost) ---\n")
cat("Correlation Coefficient (r):", cor_sat_cost, "\n\n")

# Scatterplot for SAT vs Cost
plot(college$AvgSAT, college$Cost,
     main = "Scatterplot: Average SAT vs. Total Cost",
     xlab = "Average SAT Score",
     ylab = "Total Cost ($)",
     col = "darkblue",
     pch = 19)

```

\vspace{2em}

•	Correlation Coefficient (r): 0.5374 (indicating a moderate positive linear association where higher test score tiers align with higher total costs)

\vspace{3em}




## **6. What is the linear correlation between college admission rates and average SAT scores?**

\vspace{2em}

```{r}
# --- Question 6: Correlation between AdmitRate and AvgSAT ---
cor_admit_sat <- cor(college$AdmitRate, college$AvgSAT, use = "complete.obs")

cat("--- Question 6: Correlation (Admit Rate vs SAT) ---\n")
cat("Correlation Coefficient (r):", cor_admit_sat, "\n\n")

# Scatterplot for Admit Rate vs SAT
plot(college$AdmitRate, college$AvgSAT,
     main = "Scatterplot: Admission Rate vs. Average SAT",
     xlab = "Admission Rate",
     ylab = "Average SAT Score",
     col = "darkgreen",
     pch = 19)
```

\vspace{2em}

•	Correlation Coefficient (r): -0.4221 (showing a moderate negative relationship: more selective schools with lower admission rates tend to have higher average SAT scores).

\vspace{3em}


## **7. How does average net price vary across different institutional control types?**

\vspace{2em}

```{r}
# --- Question 7: Mean Net Price by Institutional Control Type ---
mean_netprice <- tapply(college$NetPrice, college$Control, mean, na.rm = TRUE)

cat("--- Question 7: Mean Net Price by Control Type ---\n")
print(mean_netprice)

# Boxplot for Net Price by Control
boxplot(NetPrice ~ Control, data = college,
        main = "Net Price by Institutional Control Type",
        xlab = "Control Type",
        ylab = "Net Price ($)",
        col = c("lavender", "peachpuff", "lightcyan"))
```


\vspace{2em}

•	Mean Enrollment: Analyzed via standard deviation and median metrics to account for right-skewness in large university sizes.

\vspace{2em}

•	Group means show distinct net price tiers across public, private, and for-profit institutions, verified through side-by-side boxplots.

\vspace{3em}




## **8. What is the distribution and spread of undergraduate enrollment size?**

\vspace{2em}

```{r}
# --- Question 8: Summary Statistics for Undergraduate Enrollment ---
mean_enroll   <- mean(college$Enrollment, na.rm = TRUE)
median_enroll <- median(college$Enrollment, na.rm = TRUE)
sd_enroll     <- sd(college$Enrollment, na.rm = TRUE)
iqr_enroll    <- IQR(college$Enrollment, na.rm = TRUE)

cat("\n--- Question 8: Undergraduate Enrollment Statistics ---\n")
cat("Mean Enrollment:", mean_enroll, "\n")
cat("Median Enrollment:", median_enroll, "\n")
cat("Standard Deviation:", sd_enroll, "\n")
cat("IQR:", iqr_enroll, "\n")

# Histogram for Enrollment
hist(college$Enrollment,
     main = "Distribution of Undergraduate Enrollment",
     xlab = "Enrollment Size",
     col = "plum",
     border = "white")
```

\vspace{2em}

•	Mean Enrollment: Analyzed via standard deviation and median metrics to account for right-skewness in large university sizes.

\vspace{3em}




## **9. Is student graduate debt linearly correlated with total annual attendance cost?**

\vspace{2em}

```{r}
# --- Question 9: Correlation between Debt and Cost ---
cor_debt_cost <- cor(college$Debt, college$Cost, use = "complete.obs")

cat("--- Question 9: Correlation (Debt vs Cost) ---\n")
cat("Correlation Coefficient (r):", cor_debt_cost, "\n\n")

# Scatterplot for Debt vs Cost
plot(college$Cost, college$Debt,
     main = "Scatterplot: Total Cost vs. Median Debt",
     xlab = "Total Attendance Cost ($)",
     ylab = "Median Debt ($)",
     col = "darkred",
     pch = 19)
```

\vspace{2em}

•	Correlation Coefficient (r): -0.2145 (showing a weak negative relationship between stated costs and median student loan debt outcomes).

\vspace{3em}



## **10. How are four-year colleges geographically distributed across U.S. regions?**

\vspace{2em}

```{r}
# --- Question 10: Geographic Distribution by Region ---
tbl_region  <- table(college$Region)
prop_region <- prop.table(tbl_region)

cat("--- Question 10: Institutional Frequency by Region ---\n")
print(tbl_region)
print(round(prop_region, 4))

# Barplot for Geographic Region Distribution
barplot(tbl_region,
        main = "Distribution of Colleges by U.S. Region",
        xlab = "Region",
        ylab = "Number of Colleges",
        col = rainbow(length(tbl_region)),
        las = 2,
        cex.names = 0.7)
```

\vspace{2em}


•	Frequencies and proportions indicate regional density differences across the United States higher education landscape.
